blocks.content: PRIME MINISTER AND COUNCIL OF MINISTERS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 74 mandates a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister as head to aid and advise the President, whose advice is binding.
The Prime Minister is appointed by the President, and other ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister under Article 75.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People) as per Article 75(3).
The total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha (91st Amendment Act, 2003).
A minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament for six consecutive months automatically ceases to be a minister.
INTRODUCTION

blocks.content: The Prime Minister is the real executive head of the Indian State. While the President is the constitutional head,
the Prime Minister is the actual head of the government who runs the administration of the country.
The office of the Prime Minister is the most powerful political institution in India. The Prime Minister works along with the Council of Ministers to govern the nation.
The provisions related to the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers are mentioned in Articles 74 and 75 of the Indian Constitution.
ARTICLE 74 – COUNCIL OF MINISTERS
Article 74 provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.
Important points:

items:
• Advice of Council of Ministers is binding on the President
  • 42nd Constitutional Amendment made advice mandatory
  • 44th Amendment clarified that President can ask for reconsideration once, but must accept it finally
Advice of Council of Ministers is binding on the President
42nd Constitutional Amendment made advice mandatory
44th Amendment clarified that President can ask for reconsideration once, but must accept it finally

blocks.content: ARTICLE 75 – APPOINTMENT OF PRIME MINISTER
Article 75 deals with the appointment and tenure of the Prime Minister. According to this article:

items:
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President
  • The leader of the majority party in Lok Sabha becomes PM
  • Council of Ministers is appointed on PM‟s advice
  • Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President
The Prime Minister is appointed by the President
The leader of the majority party in Lok Sabha becomes PM
Council of Ministers is appointed on PM‟s advice
Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President

blocks.content: QUALIFICATIONS OF THE PRIME MINISTER
To become Prime Minister:

items:
• Must be a citizen of India
  • Must be a member of Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
  • If not a member, must become one within 6 months
Must be a citizen of India
Must be a member of Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
If not a member, must become one within 6 months

blocks.content: OATH OF OFFICE AND SECRECY
The Prime Minister takes oath before the President. Oath includes:

items:
• Faith and allegiance to Constitution
  • Upholding sovereignty and integrity
  • Performing duties faithfully
Faith and allegiance to Constitution
Upholding sovereignty and integrity
Performing duties faithfully

blocks.content: TERM OF OFFICE
The Prime Minister holds office as long as:

items:
• He enjoys majority support in Lok Sabha
  • Council of Ministers has confidence of House There is no fixed tenure.
He enjoys majority support in Lok Sabha
Council of Ministers has confidence of House There is no fixed tenure.

blocks.content: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE PRIME MINISTER
The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People.
The Prime Minister is the pivot of the entire political system. Major Powers:

items:
• Formation of Council of Ministers
  • Allocation and reshuffling of portfolios
  • Chairman of Cabinet meetings
  • Leader of Lok Sabha
  • Link between President and Cabinet
  • Chief spokesperson of Government

COUNCIL OF MINISTERS
The Council of Ministers consists of:

items:
• Cabinet Ministers
  • Ministers of State
  • Deputy Ministers

Ministers of State
Deputy Ministers

blocks.content: They collectively aid and advise the President.
CABINET
The Cabinet is the most powerful body within the Council of Ministers. Functions:

items:
• Determines government policy
  • Controls administration
  • Coordinates between departments
  • Takes major decisions

blocks.content: COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This means:

items:
• All ministers stand together
  • If Lok Sabha passes no-confidence motion, entire ministry resigns
All ministers stand together
If Lok Sabha passes no-confidence motion, entire ministry resigns

blocks.content: INDIVIDUAL RESPONSIBILITY
Each minister is individually responsible to the President.The President can remove a minister on the advice of Prime Minister.
LEGAL RESPONSIBILITY
Ministers are legally responsible for their acts. They can be prosecuted for illegal acts.
IMPORTANT SUPREME COURT CASES

items: The advice tendered by Ministers to the President cannot be inquired into in any court of law under Article 74(2).
Unlike Britain, India has no provision for the legal responsibility of a minister; executive orders do not require a minister's countersignature.
Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President (Individual Responsibility under Article 75(2)).
The word 'Cabinet' was not in the original Constitution; it was inserted into Article 352 by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.

• Ram Jawaya Kapur Case – Real executive power lies with Council of Ministers

blocks.content: CONCLUSION
The Prime Minister is the pivot of the Indian political system.
His leadership determines the stability and effectiveness of government. Though the Constitution does not describe his powers in detail,
in practice he is the most powerful executive authority in India.
